newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank merger to harm communities-groups.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank merger to harm communities-groups.

text.p: Bank customers would suffer irreperable harm if NationsBank Corp is allowed to consummate its $9.8 billion acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares Inc, a coalition of community groups told a U.S. appeals court on Friday.

The New Mexico Alliance and Inner City PRess/Community on the Move have challenged the Federal Reserve's approval of the merger in the 10th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. They are also asking the court to block the deal's consummation next week while their case is pending.

The groups submitted to the court declarations from New Mexico residents who said they fear the merger would result in local branch banks of a Boatmen's unit in New Mexico being closed. Customers would then have to drive great distances just to reach an automated teller machine, they said.
Boatmen's and its subsidiaries, including Sunwest Banks of New Mexico. operate 600 branch banks.
The groups argued that if their request for a stay is not granted and the acquisition is completed January 7, "it would be unlikely a court could or would break up the resulting NBC (NationsBank)."
The court had not handed down a decision as of Friday morning, a court clerk said.

NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C., told the court on Thursday that one of the community groups should be required to post a bond of at least $100 million if the merger is temporarily blocked. NationsBank warned that a delay of the deal would cost it $36 million a month.

The Federal Reserve Board, which approved the acquisition December 16, said on Thursday in its court papers that the community groups did not have legal standing to challenge the Fed's approval of the merger.
